ramshorn-snail.description:
Oft sitzen die Schnecken zusammen und putzen sich gegenseitig das Häuschen. Das "Lausen" hat für beide Seiten Vorteile. Keine Ahnung worüber Schnecken quatschen, aber die Schale ist sauber und der Hunger gestillt. 


Manchmal knabbern sie auch die Schale der anderen Schnecke an. Nicht immer bedeutet das Calciummangel sondern meist Überbesatz.

slate-rock.title: File:Red slate, Hatch Hill, Whitehall, Washington County, New York dtn00112.jpg
slate-rock.description:
Block of red Ordovician slate with bed, 1 inch of Limestone, green and purple slate, diagonal to the cleavage. From near Hatch Hill, Whitehall, Washington County, New York.  Photograph by T. Nelson Dale.   Plate 2 A, Slate Deposits and Slate Industry of the United States, U. S. Geological Survey Bulletin 275, 1906.
Original caption:

RED SLATE WITH BED OF LIMESTONE AND GREEN SLATE, Block of reddish slate from quarries 1 1/2 miles south of Hatch Hill, in Whitehall, N. Y., with bed of limestone bordered by green and purple slate, making a "ribbon," an inch in vertical thickness, crossing the cleavage diagonally, Scale on rule is 4 inches long.
The rock is likely from Quarry 33 shown in The slate belt of eastern New York and western Vermont by T. N. Dale, published in Nineteenth Annual Report of the United States Geological Survey to the Secretary of the Interior 1897 - 1898: Part III - Economic Geology, Annual Report 19, by: Charles D. Walcott, 1899.  Coordinates of the quarry are 43.476
